#en: I keep telling myself it is just space junk. Mech armor sloughed off some battle no one logged right, telemetry looping its own last moments until the batteries die. But the numbers in that wreck are too clean where they ought to be scarred, and bent exactly where they ought to be reliable, like someone meant to come back and finish rewriting the story and just never did. It feels like walking into a crime scene where the cleaner got interrupted mid-swipe.\n\nThe more I stare at it, the more it lines up with everything else I have tripped over by accident. A foreclosure on a farm that reversed itself while the owner was still packing. A dataslate half-buried in dust, full of draft entries that almost made it into the system. A jump node whose timing made my teeth itch even though the charts said it was fine. Little things, all of them, the kind you blame on tired clerks and lazy techs. But taken together, they look like someone started pulling on the threads of the Settled Systems a long time ago, and just got used to leaving the ends hanging.
zh: 我一直告诉自己这只是太空垃圾。机甲装甲从某场没人好好记录的战斗中剥落，遥测循环着它自己的最后时刻，直到电池耗尽。可那残骸里的数字，在该有伤痕的地方太干净，在该可靠的地方又恰好弯折，像有人打算回来把故事改写完，却始终没能回来。感觉就像走进一个凶手清理现场清到一半被打断的犯罪现场。\n\n我盯着它越久，它就越和我无意中绊到的其他一切对得上。一桩在主人还在收拾行李时就自我撤销的农场查封。一块半埋在灰尘里的数据板，满是几乎进了系统的草稿条目。一个跃迁节点，它的时序让我牙齿发痒，尽管星图说一切正常。都是些小事，那种你会归咎于疲惫文员和懒惰技工的小事。可合在一起看，就像有人在很久以前就开始拉扯定居星系群的线头，然后只是习惯了把线尾一直那么吊着。

#en: HM-6310 is still out there, hanging between beacons like a bad thought no one wants to finish. I caught its ID in a rundown dockside bar, buried in a spacer s story he swore was just a joke. Dead Navy hull, clean cuts in the comms, no scorch marks from a boarding, no beacon loop. Just silence, and a notation buried three menus deep that says "operational loss" in the kind of language auditors use when they do not want to know more.  \n\nWhat sticks with me is not the ship itself, it is the pattern around it. Convoys rerouted for "efficiency," escorts arriving a little late, patrols shifted one sector over for reasons that sound reasonable until you realize they always leave one lane thin. Then something disappears and everybody shrugs and blames raiders, or equipment, or bad luck. Nobody ever mentions the matching blackout windows or the way records get neater the closer you get to New Atlantis. Every time I bring it up, people laugh it off too fast, like they are afraid if they stop joking the truth will land somewhere between cowardice and calculation.
zh: HM-6310 还在外面，悬在信标之间，像一个没人愿意想完的坏念头。我是在一间破败的码头酒吧里撞见它的 ID 的，埋在一个太空人的故事里——他赌咒说那只是个玩笑。死海军船壳，通讯上有干净的切口，没有登船留下的烧痕，没有信标循环。只有沉默，以及深埋在三级菜单底下的一行备注，写着"作战损失"，用的是审计员在不想知道更多时才会用的那种措辞。\n\n让我挥之不去的不是那艘船本身，而是它周围的图案。运输队为"效率"被改道，护航船稍微来晚一点，巡逻因为一些听起来很合理的原因被挪到旁边的星区——直到你意识到他们总是把某条航道留薄。然后有东西消失了，大家都耸耸肩，怪劫掠者、怪设备、怪运气不好。没人提那些互相吻合的信号盲区窗口，也没人提越靠近新亚特兰蒂斯、记录就变得越整洁这件事。每次我提起，人们都笑得太快，像他们害怕一旦停止开玩笑，真相就会落在懦弱与算计之间的某个地方。

#en: Calen Rourke here, logging this before someone decides it is inconvenient and wipes the drive clean. The module is dead quiet, just fans and my own breathing, but the consoles tell a louder story than most captains ever will. I traced the data forks like any good thief would trace a payout, following the jumps where they should not bend, the packets that detoured through places no contract mentioned. Every time the trail went fuzzy, the same ship ID kept reappearing in scrubbed access notes and half-redacted audit flags from the Trade Authority. Someone thought routing that much traffic through a single cargo hauler was subtle, that if they buried it in routine freight no one would notice. Maybe they were right, for a while. But the broken beacon logs we pulled near the outer marker, the whispers in Neon's lower levels about ghost routes, and that LIST emergency broadcast everyone pretends not to remember, they all point back to the same thing: a cargo ship running too many "lucky" jumps and a pilot whose name keeps getting spoken in a lower voice every time.
zh: 我是卡伦·罗克，在有人觉得这段不方便、把驱动器擦干净之前把它记下来。模块死一般安静，只有风扇和我自己的呼吸，可控制台讲出的故事比大多数船长一辈子讲的都要响。我像个好小偷追查一笔付款那样追查那些数据分叉，顺着那些本不该弯折的跃迁、那些绕经合同从未提及之处的数据包。每次痕迹变模糊，同一个船号就会重新出现在被擦洗过的访问备注和贸易管理局打了一半涂黑标记的审计标签里。有人以为把那么多交通量穿过一艘单一货船很隐蔽，以为只要把它埋进例行货运里就没人会注意。也许在一段时间里，他们是对的。可我们在外标附近扒下来的损坏信标日志、霓虹城下层关于幽灵航线的低语，还有那则人人都假装不记得的独立盟紧急广播，全都指回同一件事：一艘跑了太多"幸运"跃迁的货船，和一名每次被提起、声音都会更低的飞行员。

#en: I have been chasing this name in the margins for months now and I am still not sure if it belongs to a person, a program, or just the way crews talk when they do not want to say what they really mean. Every time a run threads between storms that were not on the forecast, somebody shrugs and jokes that "someone upstairs has a good broker," and the room gets just a shade quieter. I am sitting in the mess of this Alliance cutter now, listening to its empty hull tick and cool, trying to piece together how a ship built to haul bounty contracts ended up holding what looks more like a weather ledger than a job list. No one left a clean record; just half-finished notes, rerouted payments, corridors of fog that keep matching the same three or four departure points. All I know for sure is that it started on a dustball outpost with cargo that should have been delayed by a week of rain and was not, then a hunter's wreck drifting way off course with storm data in its black box, then manifests from a factory town whose harvests refused to line up with their own climate reports.
zh: 我在页边空白里追这个名字追了好几个月，到现在还是不确定它到底属于一个人、一个程序，还是只是船员们不想把真话说出口时的说话方式。每当一个航次从预报里没有的风暴之间穿过去，就有人耸耸肩，开玩笑说"楼上某人有个好经纪商"，然后整个房间就安静那么一点点。此刻我坐在联盟这条切割船的食堂里，听着它空荡荡的船体在冷却时滴答作响，试图拼凑出一艘生来运送赏金合同的船怎么会装着更像气象账簿而不是任务清单的东西。没人留下过干净的记录；只有半截的笔记、被改道的付款、以及总是对得上同样三四个出发点的迷雾走廊。我唯一确定的是，它始于一座尘球前哨站——那批本该被一周降雨耽搁、结果却没有的货；接着是一个猎人的残骸严重偏航，黑匣子里装着风暴数据；再之后是一座工厂城镇的清单，它的收成死活对不上当地自己的气候报告。

#en: I came back to this rock because the noise would not shut up. You stand on the ridge and the wind is the only thing you hear, but jack into the local relay and it is like listening to a hoarder's attic: half-deleted pings, orphaned status codes, messages queued for recipients who have been dead a decade. This place should have been swept clean when the UC pulled their survey drones. It was not. Somebody skipped a step, or pretended to, and whatever he pushed through the buffer back then got caught in the same neglect.\n\nI keep replaying a fragment, a routing tag that does not match any registered ship, pulsing at intervals too regular to be ghost data. The dead agent's scribbled coordinates, that dataslate I bought off a frightened farmer, even the story about armed escorts circling a field that glowed after dark, they all bend toward the same name. Feels like everyone saw a piece and shrugged, too busy or too scared to add it up. Now I am standing in the middle of what they overlooked, wondering how long this signal has been waiting for someone to finally notice.
zh: 我回到这块岩石上，是因为那噪声不肯闭嘴。你站在山脊上，只听得到风声，可一旦接进本地的中继站，就像在听一个囤积狂的阁楼：删了一半的延时探测、成了孤儿的状况代码、排着队发给死了十年的收件人的消息。联殖撤走勘测无人机时，这地方本该被清扫干净。可它没有。有人跳过了一步，或者假装跳过了，而他当年推进缓冲区的那些东西，就被留在了同样的疏漏里。\n\n我一直在重放一个碎片：一个不属于任何登记飞船的航路标签，以过于规律的间隔脉动着，不像是幽灵数据。那名死去特工潦草写下的坐标、我从一个受惊农民手里买来的那块数据板，甚至那个关于武装护航队在夜间发光田野上空盘旋的故事，全都朝同一个名字弯过去。感觉像人人都看到了一块碎片却耸耸肩，太忙或太怕，没去加起来。如今我正站在他们忽略掉的东西当中，琢磨这信号已经等了多久，才等到有人终于注意到它。

#en: I am writing this before I lose my nerve and toss that slate back into the crate where I found it. Out here the manifests are still smeared in oil and bad handwriting, but the numbers are too neat around that one tug. Wrong hull ID, wrong routing stamp, and three different initials "fixing" the same mistake. I asked the clerk on duty who changed it; she swore she only copied what came from Gagarin. The yard boss said he signed off because a UC rep vouched for it. The rep, when I finally reached him on a laggy channel, insisted the request came from "higher up" and cut the call. Nobody owns the decision, but they all heard it from someone else first.\n\nI keep thinking about that cutter and the way its line just stops, replaced by a phantom courier that never shows on any legitimate docket. First it was a rumor from a hauler who swore a whole crew vanished off Titan. Then it was a half-burned name on a memorial wall. Now it is my own pen hovering over a ledger, deciding whether to pretend I did not see a ship quietly pushed into a graveyard route that should not exist.
zh: 我趁自己还没失去勇气、把那块数据板扔回我发现它的箱子里之前写下这些。在这外面，清单上还是油污和潦草的字迹，可那艘拖船周围的数字却整齐得过分。错的船体 ID、错的航路戳记，还有三个不同的缩写签名在"修正"同一个错误。我问当班的文员是谁改的；她赌咒说自己只是照抄加加林发来的东西。船坞老板说，是因为一名联殖代表为它担保，他才签了字。等我终于通过一条延迟严重的频道联系上那名代表，他坚称请求来自"上面"，然后挂了通讯。没人承认这个决定是自己做的，可他们全都是先从别人那里听来的。\n\n我总想着那艘切割船，想着它的航线就那么断了，被一艘从不出现在任何合法调度单上的幽灵快船取代。起初是一个运货船员的传言，他赌咒说泰坦上一整队船员消失了。然后是纪念墙上一个烧得只剩一半的名字。如今是我自己的笔悬在账簿上方，决定要不要假装没看见一艘船被悄悄推进那条本不该存在的墓地航线。

#en: I came up here to babysit a bank of half-dead sensors and drink bad coffee, not to stumble over someone else's ghost trail. The hut looks abandoned unless you know where to listen; under the wind and the creaking mast there is this steady tick of relays, software from three revisions ago still chewing on sky and ground like nobody ever told it the war was over. Half the crew cycles through, signs the maintenance sheet, never checks what the system is actually flagging. Today I dug into the ignored queue, the one that has been auto-filing anomalies as "atmospherics" for years, and there it was: a clean thermal line knifing across the ridge, too straight for weather, too smooth for wildlife, logged and time-stamped by a process nobody remembers writing. I asked around in town, and suddenly everybody's memory got real convenient; the sheriff recalls a storm, the pilot remembers "instrument noise," the bartender swears the night was quiet. The only thing not lying to me is this forgotten code, still doing its job long after the people who trusted it stopped paying attention.
zh: 我上这儿来是为了照看一排半死的传感器、喝点烂咖啡，不是来绊进别人留下的鬼痕里。那座小屋看着像废弃了，除非你知道该往哪儿听；在风声和吱呀作响的桅杆底下，是中继站稳定的滴答声——三个版本之前的软件仍在咀嚼天空和地面，像没人告诉过它战争已经结束。一半的船员轮着来，在维护表上签个字，从不检查系统究竟在标记什么。今天我挖进了那条被忽略的队列——多年来一直把异常自动归成"大气现象"的那条——然后它就在那儿：一条干净的热成像线切开山脊，太直，不像天气；太顺滑，不像野生动物；由一个没人记得谁写的过程记录并盖上了时间戳。我到镇上打听，忽然间每个人的记忆都变得非常方便；治安官记得有场风暴，飞行员记得"仪器噪声"，酒保赌咒说那晚很安静。唯一没对我说谎的，就是这段被遗忘的代码——在信任它的人早已不再留意之后很久，它仍在干着自己的活。

#en: I am not supposed to be working this, not officially. I am just the deputy they park in the field trailer to shuffle reports and pretend the border is quiet. But yesterday, while I was cleaning up an old convoy case, I pulled the raw traffic burst the UC shared with us for "coordination." Someone sliced our copy sloppily. A patch of static where their data shows a clean handoff, a time stamp that does not line up with engine burn logs, and a relay ID that should have been retired cycles ago.\n\nWhoever scrubbed it did it in a hurry and trusted nobody would look twice. They were almost right. I cross-checked that relay ID against older incidents and found it echoing behind three different "navigation failures," always the same forgotten listening post drifting just off the main corridor. The captains who survived keep blaming cheap charts or bad luck, and command is happy to let them. I have forwarded nothing yet. All I know is that the same interference that bent the buoy you are chasing once bounced through that dead UC ear, and every time it did, another convoy went dark.
zh: 我本不该碰这案子，至少不是正式地碰。我只是他们丢在野外拖车里的副手，负责整理报告、假装边境很平静。可昨天，在清理一桩旧运输队案子时，我调出了联殖为"协调"而与我们共享的原始交通数据突发。有人切我们这份副本切得很马虎。他们数据显示是一次干净交接的地方，却是一片静电；一个时间戳与引擎点火日志对不上；还有一个早该在好几个周期前就退役的中继站 ID。\n\n把它擦干净的人干得很急，笃定没人会看第二眼。他们几乎说对了。我把那个中继站 ID 与更早的事件交叉比对，发现它在三起不同的"导航故障"背后回响，永远是同一座被遗忘、漂在主走廊外不远的监听站。活下来的船长们一直怪星图太便宜或运气不好，而指挥部乐得让他们这么想。我什么都还没上报。我只知道，那股把你正在追的浮标掰弯的干扰，曾经从那只死去的联殖耳朵里弹过一次；而每一次它这么做，就有一支运输队陷入了黑暗。

#en: I am recording this from the shack before I lose my nerve and sell the whole lot to the highest bidder. The walls here sweat condensation and stolen power, a tangle of rusted antennae and half-burnt routers humming on frequencies no sane port authority checks anymore. That is why her traffic washed up on my doorstep.  \n\nIt did not come as some grand revelation. Just a double-echo in the bands, two identical convoys that never existed on any manifest, both vanishing into a dead patch where no one flies unless they have to. I followed the ghosts back through weeks of chatter, past Crimson Fleet dead-drops and Ryujin side channels, until every route rebounded off the same cold coordinate string. Spacers in back rooms keep saying Deadchannel is a myth, or a hero, or a corporate hit piece, depending on who owes who, but every retelling shaves a little truth away. The raw recordings I pulled do not care about stories. They all point to the same place the next relay in her chain, a forgotten UC node floating in the dark, where the signals go silent and the lies stop being rumors.
zh: 我在棚屋里录下这段，趁自己还没失去勇气、把整批东西卖给出价最高的人。这里的墙壁渗着冷凝水和偷来的电，一堆锈蚀天线和半烧毁的路由器在再无哪个理智的港务局会检查的频率上嗡鸣。这就是她的通讯会冲到我门口的原因。\n\n它并不是以某种宏大启示的形式到来的。只是频段里的一次双重回响，两支在任何清单上都不存在的、一模一样的运输队，双双消失在一片死寂地带——没人非去不可就不会往那儿飞的地方。我顺着这些鬼穿过好几周的闲聊往回追，穿过深红舰队的死信箱和龙神的旁路频道，直到每条航线都在同一串冰冷的坐标上弹回来。后室里的太空人一直在说"死频道"是个传说、是个英雄、或者是一篇企业抹黑稿，取决于谁欠谁的；可每一次转述都会削掉一点真相。我扒来的原始录音不在乎故事。它们全都指向同一个地方——她链条上的下一座中继站，一座漂在黑暗中、被遗忘的联殖节点，在那里信号归于寂静，谎言不再只是传言。

#en: I am writing this where no one can look over my shoulder. Out here the stars are too bright and the air is too thin for comfort, but at least the only ears are mine. I pulled the last three months of sensor sweeps from the patrol grid, buried behind routine smuggling alerts and meteor warnings. There is a pattern in the noise, a faint smear of grav interference that keeps showing up in the same narrow band of orbit. It is not on any flight plan, but it pulses with the same timing as those "isolated malfunctions" command keeps renaming.\n\nWhen I tried to bring it up in the ready room, the room went quiet in that careful way. Nobody told me I was wrong, nobody asked to see the data. They just found somewhere else to look. That is how I know I am close. The signature climbs out from the blind side of this rock and vanishes right where a derelict comms platform went missing six years ago. First the dead cache, then the jump-scarred freighter, now a grav shadow in empty orbit, all sharing the same geometry. Whatever she is doing, she is walking the same invisible line every time.
zh: 我在没人能从背后偷看的地方写下这些。在这外面，星星太亮，空气太稀薄，谈不上舒服，但至少只有我这一双耳朵。我从巡逻网格里调出最近三个月的传感器扫描，它们被埋在例行的走私警报和流星警告后面。噪声里有图案：一处微弱的重力干扰涂抹，反复出现在同一条狭窄的轨道带里。它不在任何飞行计划上，却以和那些被指挥部一再改名的"孤立故障"相同的时序脉动着。\n\n我试着在待命室里提起它时，房间以一种谨慎的方式安静下来。没人说我错了，没人要求看数据。他们只是找到了别的方向去看。就是这样我才知道自己离得近了。那特征从这块岩石的背面爬上来，恰好在六年前一座弃用的通讯平台失踪的地方消失。先是那个死缓存，然后是那艘带着跃迁伤痕的货船，现在又是空轨道上的一道重力暗影，全都共享同样的几何。不管她在做什么，她每次都走在同一条看不见的线上。
